clue.text: Professor delayed accepting without introduction loud waster

indicators.note: accepting means one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: delayed means late, behind time

indicators.note: without introduction tells us to drop the opening letter of the word that loud stands for

parts.note: big can describe a voice that is loud or resonant

explanation.surface: An academic who turns up late is dismissed as a noisy good-for-nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: BIG can describe a loud voice; once its opening letter is dropped, 'accepting' puts what is left inside the word for delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A spendthrift who squanders money recklessly is a dissolute, wasteful person.

clue.text: Calm those upset about nothing

indicators.note: about here means placed around another piece
upset signals that the letters of those are knocked into a new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone reassuring people who have been distressed over a trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns THOSE into SOTHE, and 'about' wraps it round O after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify or settle someone's nerves is to make them tranquil again.

clue.text: Plain cold? I call in shivering

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: shivering suggests the letters trembling out of place into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A patient reports a simple chill, ringing the surgery while trembling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shivering' rearranges I CALL IN into LINICAL, placed after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinical can mean austere and unadorned, as in a stark, bare room.

clue.text: Rather kind old fellow

parts.note: a kind is a sort or type
OF is the abbreviation for old fellow

explanation.surface: Describing an elderly man as fairly pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a casual hedge meaning somewhat or to some degree.

clue.text: Hasty MP broke and close to bankruptcy agreement

indicators.note: broke is a past form of break, so the letters are smashed and reassembled
close to picks the closing letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An impulsive politician went bust and was near to bankruptcy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' rearranges HASTY MP into SYMPATH; 'close to' gives the Y ending bankruptcy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sympathy can mean accord or harmony of feeling between people.

clue.text: Glass featured in shop always

indicators.note: featured in means the answer appears within the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A display item always on show in a shop window.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'shOP ALways'.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal glass is a milky, translucent kind of glassware named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Bird present in pub left

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bar is a pub
present as in the current time means now

explanation.surface: A gift was left behind at the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift, but it is the time sense, and 'in' puts it inside the pub plus left.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale owl that often roosts in farm buildings is a familiar species.

clue.text: Overwhelmed and concerning others?

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: something about others is placed next to, not on, your own self.
explanation.definitionFit: Distraught with emotion is the idiom; read literally the phrase means alongside your own self, so about other people.

clue.text: Copy I'm changing about 50 of the games?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters surround another piece
changing tells us the letters of copy and I'm are altered into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Imitating something with fifty attempts, perhaps at a sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges the copy-and-I'm letters to OYMPIC, and 'about' wraps them round the Roman fifty. The question mark admits the definition is adjectival.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the international sporting festival held every four years.

clue.text: Company on the case get confused importing European dairy product

indicators.note: importing means bringing another piece inside
confused means the letters are jumbled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A firm working on a muddled investigation brings in a foreign product from the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges the case-and-get letters, and 'importing' takes in the European letter; 'on' puts the company abbreviation above in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft white curd made from skimmed milk is a familiar product of the creamery.

clue.text: Second fat teen rampaging around yard? Precaution needed

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters enclose another piece
rampaging means running wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An overweight youngster running wild in the garden needs something to break a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rampaging' rearranges the fat-teen letters, and 'around' wraps them round the yard abbreviation, giving AFETYNET; 'needed' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A backup that guards against disaster is a protective measure, literally a mesh below acrobats.

clue.text: Early film presenting very religious group

parts.note: pi is informal shorthand for pious, very religious
a lot is a group or set of things

explanation.surface: An early movie is shown to a devout congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is an old British school slang word for sanctimonious.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial episode made before a television series is commissioned is an initial screening.

clue.text: Organised campaign's energy

explanation.definitionFit: A drive is a concerted effort to achieve something, and also vigour or ambition.

clue.text: After a holiday in Costa Rica, recall fine restaurant

indicators.note: After tells us the reversed piece comes at the end
in means these pieces sit inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: CR is the international code for Costa Rica
a fete is a festival or holiday celebration

indicators.note: recall means calling back, so the piece for fine is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or fine

explanation.surface: Back from a Central American trip, someone remembers an excellent eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-rate, so fine is A1, read as the letters A and I; 'recall' turns them round and 'After' places them at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service eating place is a kind of informal dining establishment.

clue.text: Horny type caught between money and romantic inspiration?

indicators.note: between means the letter for caught sits in the middle of the other two pieces

parts.note: rhino is old British slang for money
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: An amorous person trapped between cash and passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny' looks like lust, but it means having a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: This thick-skinned African or Asian beast carries one or two horns on its snout.

clue.text: Lola and Ron trained having continuing success

indicators.note: trained means the letters are drilled into a new formation

explanation.surface: Two named people coached together and keep winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges LOLA RON.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a streak of good fortune, one triumph after another.

clue.text: One using stops in church?

parts.note: stops sounds like halting or punctuation, but these are the knobs that select pipe ranks on a church instrument

explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' suggests bringing things to a halt; the musician pulls stops to choose ranks of pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: The keyboard player at services pulls knobs called stops on the pipe instrument.

clue.text: Reportedly, consider team on edge of path

indicators.note: Reportedly tells us we want a word as it is spoken rather than as written

parts.note: to weigh something up is to consider it
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: Someone said to be thinking about a team standing beside the track.
explanation.walkthrough: WEIGH said out loud gives WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The verge beside a road or track is the border along its margin.

clue.text: Time to probe a variety of wine not properly examined

indicators.note: to probe means to push into, so one piece enters the other
a variety of suggests a mixed version of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Being given time to investigate a wine whose kind was not tasted carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a variety of' rearranges the wine-not letters into WENINTO, and 'to probe' pushes the time letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To go into a matter is to investigate it thoroughly.

clue.text: Unfading English priest returns with endless energy amazingly

indicators.note: returns means the word goes back, read in reverse

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a priest

indicators.note: amazingly suggests the letters are astonishingly scrambled
endless means drop the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An English cleric comes back full of tireless vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns REV into VER; 'endless' cuts energy to ENERG and 'amazingly' rearranges that into GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that keep their leaves all year stay perpetually fresh, hence lasting.

clue.text: Do better than former top player on radio

indicators.note: on radio tells us the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: ex is former, and a seed is a top-ranked player in a tournament

explanation.surface: A one-time star athlete outperforms others while commentating on the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: EX-SEED said out loud gives EXCEED. A seed is a highly ranked player, as at Wimbledon.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or outdo someone is to go beyond their level.

clue.text: Tail missing from inferior Chinese dog

indicators.note: Tail missing from means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: poor means inferior in quality

explanation.surface: A substandard Chinese breed of dog without a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail missing from' turns POOR into POO.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooch is informal slang for a canine pet.

clue.text: View obscuring front wing

indicators.note: obscuring front means the opening letter is hidden away

parts.note: a view is an opinion or belief

explanation.surface: A viewpoint that blocks the front of a building's extension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscuring front' removes the O from OPINION. 'wing' looks architectural but is the bird sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinion is the outer part of a bird's flight limb, or the whole of it in poetry.

clue.text: Heading west, river fringes grand Scottish place

indicators.note: fringes means surrounds, forming the border around a piece
in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: the Nile is Africa's great river
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A river flowing west forms the border of a magnificent estate in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading west' reverses NILE to ELIN, which 'fringes' puts around G. ELGIN is a town in Moray, north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a cathedral town in Moray, in the north-east of Scotland.

clue.text: Crew making joke about name

indicators.note: about means surrounding another piece

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A team cracking a joke about someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts GAG around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a group of workers or companions, like a team.

clue.text: Line Celt developed to ensnare European customers

indicators.note: to ensnare means to trap something inside
developed means the letters are worked up into a new form

explanation.surface: An ancient Briton drew up a queue to catch a foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges the line-and-Celt letters, and 'to ensnare' traps the European letter inside them; a Celt is an ancient Briton or Gaul.
explanation.definitionFit: A clientele is the body of patrons of a business.

clue.text: Expertise shown by exquisite society in the home counties

parts.note: exquisite means fine, of high quality

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the home counties are the counties around London, in the South East, SE

explanation.surface: Skill displayed by a refined set around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's South East (SE); 'in' puts S inside SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is refined skill or delicacy in handling something.

clue.text: Pair extremely taken with maths exercise, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the pieces are taken as they sound, not as spelt

parts.note: extremely is too and a maths exercise is a sum; taken with joins them, giving too sum

explanation.surface: Two people very absorbed in arithmetic homework.
explanation.walkthrough: TOO SUM said out loud gives TWOSOME; 'taken with' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a couple, two people together.
